items.followUp: Differentiate between renewable energy and non-renewable energy.

rubric.why: Identifies magma as molten rock beneath Earth’s surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that magma is molten rock beneath the Earth’s surface.

rubric.why: Identifies geothermal energy as heat from inside Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that geothermal energy is heat energy from the interior of the Earth.

modelAnswer: Magma is hot molten rock present beneath the Earth’s surface.
Geothermal energy is heat energy obtained from the interior of the Earth.

items.followUp: Explain how the least count of a screw gauge is found and how it is used to measure a small diameter.

rubric.why: States what a screw gauge is used to measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that a screw gauge measures small lengths, such as the diameter of a wire or thickness of a sheet.

rubric.why: Describes the screw gauge’s essential construction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its frame, anvil and spindle, or identifying its main and circular scales.

rubric.why: Defines the pitch of the screw gauge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pitch is the distance moved by the spindle in one complete rotation.

rubric.why: Gives the least-count relation or the measurement-reading formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for least count = pitch divided by the number of circular-scale divisions, or for the correct reading formula.

modelAnswer: A screw gauge is used to measure very small lengths, such as the diameter of a wire or the thickness of a sheet.
It consists of a U-shaped frame, an anvil, a movable spindle, a main scale and a circular scale; the ratchet helps apply uniform pressure.
The pitch is the distance moved by the spindle in one complete rotation.
Least count = pitch ÷ number of divisions on the circular scale.
Measurement = main-scale reading + (circular-scale reading × least count).

items.followUp: A force of 150 N acts for 0.20 s. Find the change in momentum.

rubric.why: Identifies the given change in momentum and force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Δp = 22 N s and F = 200 N.

rubric.why: Uses the force–momentum relation and rearranges it to find time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using F = Δp/t and rearranging to t = Δp/F.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given values into the rearranged formula with appropriate units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 22 N s and 200 N into t = Δp/F.

rubric.why: Gives the correct time with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct result, 0.11 s.

modelAnswer: Given: Change in momentum, Δp = 22 N s; force, F = 200 N.
Formula: F = Δp/t, so t = Δp/F.
Substitution: t = (22 N s)/(200 N) = 0.11 s.
Answer: The required time is 0.11 s.

items.followUp: A Vernier callipers has 10 vernier divisions equal to 9 main-scale divisions. If one main-scale division is 1 mm, find its least count.

rubric.why: States that least count is the difference between one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving LC = 1 MSD − 1 VSD or stating the equivalent difference.

rubric.why: Gives the relation for the least count when the vernier divisions are related to the main-scale divisions, or explains what the least count represents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating LC = 1 MSD/n for the stated division relation, or that the least count is the smallest length measurable by the callipers.

modelAnswer: The least count is the difference between the value of one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division: LC = 1 MSD − 1 VSD.
If n vernier divisions equal (n − 1) main-scale divisions, then LC = 1 MSD/n; it is the smallest length that can be measured by the callipers.
